text:
omar: heads up — during the onprem soak tests I hit a conntrack surge in the priv-edge cluster, some nodes started dropping outbound keystore handshakes. Repro steps + logs below. Anyone seen this after the RBAC agent rollout?
jen: can you paste the exact error? conntrack OOM or iptables drop?
omar: here's the node dmesg / conntrack output:
```
$ sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
131072
$ sudo conntrack -S
cpu=4 used=131070 found=0
# lots of TIME_WAIT entries from keystore-agent->kms:443
```
jen: looks like conntrack exhausted. Are we opening many ephemeral outbound sockets? which keystore version?
omar: keystore-agent v0.9.1 (deployed via helm canary), RBAC change rolled 3 hours earlier (svcaccount scoping). Could be client not reusing keep-alives.
nana: typo check: "ana" not "nana".
nana: (ignore)
nana: wait sorry — ignore the previous line.
nana: :eyes: thanks. This ties into KMS handshake failures we saw in telemetry. Two quick asks: 1) add audit log markers for `keystore-agent:connect` 2) check if the RBAC change removed `system:node-proxy` permissions that allowed agent to use long-lived connection
raj: quick fix: bump `nf_conntrack_max` and enable `tcp_tw_recycle`? (don't enable in prod) Better to fix connection reuse at agent.
omar: for experiments I increased nf_conntrack to 500k and conntrack freed up, services recovered.
nana: we should treat this as vuln/operational risk. Proposed actions:
- add audit event tag on connect attempts (keystore-agent)
- add egress policy to only allow keystore-agent -> kms fqdn:443
- instrument agent to use HTTP/2 or connection pooling
- run a small regression test before RBAC changes
jen: agree. Also KMS integration: are we doing TLS SNI or mTLS? If it's client TLS only, short-lived sockets are expensive.
omar: currently TLS with server certs (client TLS only). mTLS rollout is gated.
nana: I'll open a short incident drill ticket and assign severity P2. Need timeline for rollbacks and forensic logs.
security-bot: Incident created: #INC-2024-2117 (P2) — assigned to ana, omar. Audit collection in progress.
raj: quick diagnostic commands:
```
kubectl get pods -n priv-edge -o wide
kubectl logs -l app=keystore-agent -n priv-edge --tail=200
sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
```
omar: also found an audit log sample showing failed decrypt calls during the spike:
[2024-02-12T09:14:22Z] keystore-agent connect error: tls handshake failed -> read tcp 10.12.4.5:49152->kms.internal:443: connection reset by peer
ana: for the change control, new RBAC rollback criteria:
- >1% auth failures to keystore in 5m window OR conntrack usage >80% for 3m
jen: can we add automated rollback to helm canary? so we never reach cluster-wide regen.
omar: yes. I'll push a canary that instruments keepalive and report back.
nana: also add audit pipeline retention to 90 days for keystore auth events (forensics).
raj: note: netpol to restrict egress will also prevent lateral fallthrough. sample yaml:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: keystore-egress-only
  namespace: priv-edge
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: infra-services
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: kms-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
nana: Good. After we stabilise, let's run a tabletop sim where we intentionally break keep-alives and confirm fallbacks (Dedicated fallback, model variant). Also confirm KMS key rotation plan in Private (HSM integration).
omar: ack. I'll post initial canary results in ~2h.
jen: thanks. :thumbsup: 
security-bot: Update: Audit logs collected and archived to secure S3. Next steps assigned."
